question: In the DX-Scorecard MBR redesign, which new surfaces (Reviews entry screen, collection screen, builder, Preview) are gated behind import.meta.env.DEV like today's MbrBuilderView, and which — e.g. viewing a published month via the existing #locked/<id> LockedView path invoked by the "View" button — remain available in the read-only production build?
recommendation: Gate every authoring/editing surface of the redesign — the Reviews entry screen, the collection screen, the builder, and the pre-publish Preview — behind import.meta.env.DEV exactly as MbrBuilderView and EditRosterView are today, so Rollup dead-code-eliminates them and the build-purity test stays green. Keep only the read-only published-month view served by the existing #locked/<id> LockedView route (the destination of the "View" button) in the production bundle; it ships because it renders committed, immutable snapshot JSON with no write path.
supporting_points: The repo's binding rule (CONTEXT.md 'Dev-only surfaces', ADR-003) is that editing exists only under `vite dev`: every editing surface is wrapped in an `import.meta.env.DEV` guard so Rollup tree-shakes it out, and `src/build-purity.test.ts` runs a real production build asserting no editing markers leak. In App.tsx the `edit` and `mbr` routes are reachable ONLY inside the `if (import.meta.env.DEV)` branch (and a stray dev hash in prod falls back to Default). The new authoring surfaces (Reviews entry, collection, builder, Preview) all write via the DEV-only `/__data//__mbr//__collect` bridge in `scripts/dev-write-plugin.ts` + DEV-gated `src/lib/devWrite.ts`, so they belong behind the same gate.

LockedView is fundamentally different: it is the shareable, read-only `#locked/<id>` route whose key is a committed, immutable snapshot id resolved from checked-in JSON so the link survives redeploys (ADR-002/ADR-004). It renders `getSnapshot(id)` with no editing controls and no write endpoint, and in App.tsx it sits in the always-on `switch` outside the DEV guard alongside Default/Model — so the "View" button that navigates to a published month keeps working in the static production build.

This split preserves the existing invariant with zero new machinery: authoring is DEV-only and disappears from `dist/`, while viewing a locked/published month is public. The Preview surface, despite feeling 'view-like', is a pre-publish authoring step (it previews an unpublished draft before it is locked) and must be DEV-gated; the post-publish read-only equivalent that production users get is precisely the LockedView `#locked/<id>` render, so no viewing capability is lost by keeping it out of the prod bundle.
